title: Entropy mitigation runbook — draft (weekly)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft of an operation runbook and experiment plan to reduce long-tail latency and capacity entropy across the GPU fleet. 'Entropy' here = unpredictable degradation over a 24–72 hour window driven by cache fragmentation, micro-preemptions, and cross-tenant resource churn. The doc collects observed signals, short-term mitigations, and a small set of conservative experiments to validate tactics before we bake them into the main capacity runbook.

Context / Why now:
- Last three weeks we saw an upward drift in p95/p99 for low-priority hosted customers in us-west and eu-central during weekday spikes (see INFRA-5791).
- Root traces show combination of cold-kv-cache misses (prefix cache eviction), frequent GPU preemptions in a subset of spot-like nodes, and suboptimal batch packing for short sequences.
- Existing priming and prewarming scripts mitigate cold-starts but do not account for fragmentation at queue-level or cross-region spill that amplifies tail.

Observed signals and quick captures (standup blips):
- 2028-11-03 09:12 UTC: 15% increase in p99 tokens/sec latency for hosted-api route /generate in us-west-2 (Liam).
- 2028-11-05 17:40 UTC: small cluster of NVLink nodes preempted then reattached causing a 20s window of high reroute (Chen).
- Persistent ~8% degraded throughput on short-seq requests (<128 tokens) due to batcher underutilization (Marisol).

Proposed mitigation tiers (immediate -> medium -> long):
1) Immediate (safest, config-only, low blast radius):
   - Shorten eviction aggressiveness for prefix/KV caches on hosted-api critical routes from 60m -> 90m. (Config change, rollout 10% then 50%)
   - Add a 30s randomized jitter to batcher flush to avoid synchronized flush storms across nodes.
   - Tag preemptible nodes in west-2 as "probation" for scale-down decisions; avoid draining them mid-peak windows.
2) Medium (experiments, low-risk):
   - Implement a lightweight queue-lease: on allocation, give a 5–15 minute soft reservation to stabilize local caches for high-traffic routes. If underutilized, allow backfill at tail latency thresholds.
   - Introduce a probabilistic prewarm job that targets the top 10% of model routes by QPS with per-region controls. Use sampling to limit cost ~<3% baseline.
3) Long (architectural, requires validation):
   - Cross-node cache sharing API: prototype a bloom-filter based prefix-sharing gossip to reduce duplication of warm prefixes across nodes.
   - Batch packing heuristics via online RL-lite: score incoming requests for pack affinity to balance latency and token-efficiency.

Metrics to monitor (dashboards to add):
- Route-level p50/p95/p99 token-gen latency (by region, model, priority).
- KV cache hit ratio (per-node and per-route) and median TTL post-eviction.
- Preemption frequency per AZ and duration to reattach.
- Batcher occupancy distribution (percent requests in full batches vs solo flush).

Experiment plan (two-week rolling cadence):
Week 0 (canary):
- Change: Increase cache TTL to 90m on hosted-api for /generate route. Rollout: 5% nodes -> monitor 2h -> 20% -> monitor 24h.
- Hypothesis: p99 reduces by >10% without >1% increase in cost.
Week 1 (probe):
- Start queue-lease pilot on a single small cluster in eu-central for route /chat-complete. Lease = 10m. Backfill allowed after 4m underutilization.
- Instrument: additional tracing for lease collisions and eviction counts.
Week 2 (scale):
- Activate probabilistic prewarm for top-3 routes in us-west with sampling 5% -> 15% if no regression.

Rollback criteria (hard stops):
- Any canary that increases p99 by >15% or increases error rate by >0.2% for the route.
- Any config change that raises cost by >2% measured at account-level in the region.

Daily standup notes (this week):
- Mon: Reviewed INFRA-5791 stack traces; agreement to test TTL bump. Action: Asha to raise canary patch and coordinate with release-eng.
- Tue: Marisol demoed batcher profiling; found a frequent 7–12ms scheduling jitter when node-local queue depth >50. Action: Marisol + Chen to add telemetry.
- Wed: Liam ran prewarm cost micro-sim and found sampling 5% increases GPU utilization by 1.8% but reduces cold-kv misses by 12%. Action: validate on live traffic.
- Thu: Ops rotation reported 2 AZ preemptions in us-west suspected to be maintenance windows; added a temporary AZ-tag to avoid scheduled scale-down.
- Fri: Retro: need clearer ownership on runbook changes and a quick rollback channel.

Open questions / unknowns:
- What is the optimal lease length for different model sizes? (small models likely <8m, large >20m)
- How do we cost-allocate prewarm activity across hosted vs dedicated customers?
- Is there any interference with Dedicated autoscaler policies when we add leases? Need SRE and Dedicated-eng input.

Action items (owner — due):
- Asha: push TTL change canary PR and coordinate 5% rollout (due 2028-11-09).
- Marisol: add batcher occupancy telemetry + synthetic test that reproduces 7–12ms jitter (due 2028-11-12).
- Chen: prototype queue-lease wiring in the allocator daemon (sketch, no rollout) and post to PR (due 2028-11-16).
- Liam: run cost-sensitivity simulation for probabilistic prewarm at sampling rates [1,5,10,20]% and produce summary (due 2028-11-13).

Quick checklist for any canary rollout (ops checklist):
- Verify smoke tests for route pass locally and in canary cluster.
- Ensure oncall is paged for the canary window and aware of rollback criteria.
- Create ephemeral dashboard tile for live monitoring for first 24h.
- Repo the config change with clear revert commit.

Appendix: references and ticket links
- JIRA-INFRA-5791: "us-west p99 drift analysis" (investigation thread)
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/entropy-mitigation
- Slack history: #gpu-ops 2028-11-03..2028-11-08

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally terse — the goal is to capture the set of low-risk levers we can try this month. Please add concrete measurement ideas next to each mitigation we list (use comments on the doc).

End of note.
